val2 = "5"
total = val1 + val2
print("Total weight:", total)
case1.buggyCode:
val1 = "10"
val2 = "5"
total = val1 + val2
print(total)
case1.fixedCode:

val2 = 5
total = val1 + val2

storyComparison.storyText: Robot scale displayed '105kg' when 10kg and 5kg boxes were placed together.
storyComparison.pythonText: val1 = "10" and val2 = "5" join together as text "105" instead of adding numbers 10 + 5.

discovery.title: Logical Error
discovery.definition: The program runs completely without crashing, but produces an incorrect result because the calculation rule is wrong.
discovery.realLifeConnection: The robot scale displayed '105' because two text digits were stuck together instead of adding physical weights.
discovery.pythonConnection: Quotes around numbers ('10') make Python treat them as text strings. Removing quotes allows mathematical addition.
discovery.memoryTip: Logical errors don't crash your code—they just give wrong answers!

case1.hint: Look at lines 1 and 2. Are the numbers wrapped in quotes ("10") or plain numbers (10)?
case1.solution: Remove the quotation marks around 10 and 5 so Python adds them as numbers.
case1.summarySentence: Quotes around numbers caused text concatenation instead of numeric addition.

case2.codeSnippet:
red_time = 8
blue_time = 12
is_winner = red_time > blue_time
print("Red wins:", is_winner)
case2.buggyCode:
red_time = 8
blue_time = 12
is_winner = red_time > blue_time
print("Red wins:", is_winner)
case2.fixedCode:
red_time = 8
blue_time = 12
is_winner = red_time < blue_time
print("Red wins:", is_winner)

storyComparison.storyText: Red Car finished in 8s (faster), but Blue Car (12s) was awarded the trophy.
storyComparison.pythonText: The comparison operator > checked for bigger time instead of smaller time.

discovery.title: Logical Error
discovery.definition: The code executes smoothly, but the comparison condition produces an unexpected result.
discovery.realLifeConnection: In a race, lower time means faster speed. The scoreboard used > instead of <.
discovery.pythonConnection: 8 < 12 evaluates to True, but 8 > 12 evaluates to False.
discovery.memoryTip: In race timing, smaller numbers win!

case2.hint: In race timing, a faster car has a SMALLER time. Check the operator sign on line 3.
case2.solution: Change red_time > blue_time to red_time < blue_time.
case2.summarySentence: Using > instead of < declared the slower car as the winner.

case3.beforeOutput: SyntaxError: expected ':' at end of if statement

storyComparison.storyText: The electronic display froze instantly before showing student report cards.
storyComparison.pythonText: Python stopped execution immediately because line 3 was missing a colon (:).

discovery.title: Syntax Error
discovery.definition: Python cannot read or execute the program because a punctuation or grammar rule was broken.
discovery.realLifeConnection: Like a missing period at the end of a sentence or a misspelled highway sign.
discovery.pythonConnection: If statements in Python require a colon (:) at the end of the condition line.
discovery.memoryTip: Syntax errors crash before the code even starts running!

case3.hint: Look at the end of line 3. What punctuation mark is missing after rohan?
case3.solution: Add a colon (:) to the end of line 3: if ananya > rohan:
case3.summarySentence: Missing colon (:) on the if statement caused an immediate Syntax Error.

storyComparison.storyText: Conductor tried to scan Coach C, but the scanner had only 2 coaches in memory.
storyComparison.pythonText: Line 2 attempted to access index 2 when the list only had indices 0 and 1.

discovery.title: Runtime Error
discovery.definition: The program starts running fine, but crashes midway when trying to perform an impossible action.
discovery.realLifeConnection: The conductor reached for a 3rd coach that was not logged in the register.
discovery.pythonConnection: Python list indices start at 0. Accessing index 2 of a 2-item list causes an IndexError.
discovery.memoryTip: Runtime errors happen while the program is actively running!

case4.hint: Line 1 only has 2 coaches listed. Add "Coach C" to the list on line 1.
case4.solution: Change coaches = ["Coach A", "Coach B"] to coaches = ["Coach A", "Coach B", "Coach C"].
case4.summarySentence: Accessing index 2 on a 2-item list caused an IndexError Runtime Error.

discovery.title: Runtime Error
discovery.definition: The computer attempted a mathematical operation that is impossible in math rules.
discovery.realLifeConnection: The clinic computer tried to average temperatures across 0 patients.
discovery.pythonConnection: Dividing any number by zero in Python causes an immediate ZeroDivisionError.

discovery.title: Logical Error
discovery.definition: The decision condition inverted the comparison operator, routing good items to reject bins.
discovery.realLifeConnection: Passing solar lights were diverted to scrap bins.
discovery.pythonConnection: 85 < 80 evaluates to False, triggering the else block.
discovery.memoryTip: Always double check your < and >= comparison signs!

case6.hint: Passing items must score 80 or higher. Change < 80 to >= 80 on line 2.
case6.solution: Change is_pass = score < 80 to is_pass = score >= 80.
